title: Local Observation And Remote Server Boundary
summary: Separate source observation from central coordination so local-first Shin can later serve remote clients without claiming access to an unseen worktree.
desktopDirection: Observer will generate local metrics and provide a Desktop Dashboard plus tray presence. It may display authorized Server state so a separate Server UI remains optional. Layout, framework, IPC and packaging are deferred; see shin-observer-desktop-plan-v1.

roles.observer: A bounded native component near the source. It is not an LLM agent, a second ranker or an unrestricted remote execution agent.
roles.server: Coordinates authorized projects and clients, stores history and assessments, and exposes common API services for Desktop/CLI/future MCP clients. A separately hosted UI is not required by the architecture.
roles.core: Shared deterministic operations used locally or by the server according to explicit data placement.

deploymentModes.visibility: Registered local roots and authorized locally available evidence.
deploymentModes.processes: Observer and its local Core remain usable independently when Server or PostgreSQL is stopped or unreachable.

deploymentModes.visibility: Registered local roots and authorized locally available evidence.
deploymentModes.processes: Optional same-process development convenience only; it cannot claim independent offline Observer continuity.

deploymentModes.visibility: Server-owned checkouts and explicitly supplied Git/CI/runtime observations only.
deploymentModes.limitation: Cannot assess an unrelated developer's uncommitted worktree.

deploymentModes.visibility: Authorized observations from a registered source host.
deploymentModes.limitation: Remote state is producer-observed and current only within its explicit scope and age.

proactivity.example: A source change invalidates a prior observation; related evidence is marked for reassessment; UI and agent clients receive an Impact recommendation. A referenced test is not automatically run.
proactivity.explicitWatchPolicy: Watch attachment is opt-in. Read-only observation never silently becomes automatic build or document repair.

observationIdentity.rootMapping: Machine-local canonical roots are mapped to authorized project/worktree identities. A path string supplied by a remote client cannot grant filesystem access.
observationIdentity.versioning: Negotiate an explicit observation schema/capability set; incompatible evidence is rejected, never silently reinterpreted.
observationIdentity.truthBoundary: An authenticated sender identifies a producer, not a truthful or complete statement. Missing bytes or missing scope cannot be inferred from hashes alone.

watchAndReconciliation.events: Filesystem notifications are invalidation hints. Coalescing, overflow, root replacement and missed intervals require bounded rescan or an explicit incomplete result.
watchAndReconciliation.recheck: Keep content verification separate from notification delivery. Revalidate inputs around evidence creation; concurrent edits cannot be labeled a coherent current snapshot.
watchAndReconciliation.resume: Persist a bounded durable outbox and delivery cursor while local Core stays useful offline. Explicitly reconcile producer epoch, acknowledged sequence, profile and base revision after reconnect. Duplicates are idempotent; gaps and obsolete epochs cannot silently update current state. Competing shared-base proposals become visible conflicts, not last-writer-wins updates.
watchAndReconciliation.time: Do not rely on equal clocks across hosts. Capture time, receive time, skew policy and TTL assessment stay visible.
watchAndReconciliation.availability: Heartbeat proves connectivity only. Missing Observer, expired evidence and source drift have separate states: offline, unknown, expired or stale rather than a permanent green result.

dataPlacement.policy: Source and index stay on the observed host; local Core returns only authorized bounded evidence.
dataPlacement.serverLimit: Without the Observer, the server cannot execute a fresh source query against that worktree.

dataPlacement.policy: A source-bearing publication is transferred only after explicit export authorization and integrity checks.
dataPlacement.serverLimit: An exported snapshot is immutable historical content until a newer source observation establishes its relation to the live worktree.

transport.direction: Prefer an authenticated outbound Observer connection; do not require an inbound developer-machine port.
transport.security: Require authorization per route and operation; TLS for non-loopback traffic; revoke compromised identities without granting arbitrary remote paths.
transport.buffering: Bound queues and local spool, use backpressure and expose discarded/coalesced telemetry. Important gaps require resync; they are not hidden as successful delivery.
transport.delivery: Use sequence/cursor identity and idempotent processing. Do not promise exactly-once network transport.
transport.payload: Raw source, full queries, credentials and chat transcripts are excluded from default observations. Metadata export still requires a reviewed disclosure policy.

sources.use: Dropped events and root changes require explicit reconciliation.
Architectural analogy for local observation and a central backend, not a claim that OpenTelemetry provides Shin source indexing.

remoteHostValidation.topology: Observer and Server on separate hosts with a dedicated test PostgreSQL database.
remoteHostValidation.isolation: Do not replace the stable Shin checkout, binary, indexes, skills, production databases or default listener on either host.
remoteHostValidation.prerequisite: Independent local Observer/Core mode passes correctness and resource gates, including projects without Git; network protocol and permissions are reviewed before deployment.
remoteHostValidation.performanceBoundary: No network or service throughput result is claimed by this documentation task.
